exposure: number of babies (second, third or more vs. first)
outcome: psychometric properties of Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale (PASS)
cohort: The study enrolled 295 Lebanese women attending postnatal checkups at four clinics 4-6 weeks after delivery.
finding: Higher postpartum anxiety, insomnia, hypotension during pregnancy, and multiparity were significantly associated with higher postpartum depression, while higher postpartum depression was associated with higher postpartum anxiety, and planned pregnancy and regular baby eating were associated with lower postpartum anxiety.
